summary: Match opt-in person attention membership to the current native lowercase assignee range

replay.detail: Normal Store open and production attention reads retain their existing computation. No production replay or backfill is introduced. Explicit unpublished operator installation uses bounded source and maintenance pages.

schema.detail: The opt-in person operator uses the lowercase assignee range index and a new person-fences.v3 fingerprint. An older disposable operator lifetime cannot certify the new definition. No numeric Store schema transition or production installation is introduced.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rule, shared projection digest or fleet coordination change. These disposable operator tables are not activated in production by this change.

compatibility.detail: Native production selection, public attention IDs, actions, recorded episodes and clock wrappers remain unchanged. Legacy uppercase PERSON assignments were already absent from the native reader; the opt-in operator now agrees.

downtime.detail: No additional service interruption or production startup work is introduced.

manual.detail: Existing installations require no manual action. Shared runtime integration and complete source certification are required before any future activation.

recovery.detail: Production remains on the existing full reader. Opt-in family output is disposable and never authoritative; unavailable or unflushed families reject reads rather than replaying from a GET or returning partial Ready output. Real Store lifecycle controls verify persisted identity across reopen and retain the primitive registry fence after checkpoint deletion; replacement certification remains installer-owned.
